title: Stability Orienteering: Field Guide and Cross-Team Collab Sprint
body:
Purpose and intent:
This is a practical, bottom-up field guide to run a 6-week cross-functional stability sprint focused on SLO operationalization for model-serving endpoints. The intent is not to re-specify SLOs but to create repeatable, low-friction runbooks, quick experiments, and escalation handoffs so feature teams can adopt service-level thinking with minimal friction.

Who should read this:
- SREs partnering with feature teams owning model endpoints
- Platform engineers (serving/runtime) who need clearer guardrails
- Product/PMs who depend on predictable latency/cost SLAs
- Solutions & Customer Success for high-touch customer onboarding

High-level goals (6 weeks):
1) Get 3 pilot model-serving routes from "no SLO" to "observable + error budget policy".
2) Deliver a lightweight synthetic test harness and a canary policy per route.
3) Reduce P99 tail risk exposure via targeted mitigations (KV caching, prefix cache, batching settings).
4) Create an ops playbook for brownouts + automatic fallback chaining for model variants.

Sprint cadence and roles:
- Sprint length: 6 weeks (12 x 1-week iterations = 6 two-week workblocks but run weekly checkpoints)
- Core leads: SRE lead (Ethan), Platform lead (Aisha), Feature PM (Daniel)
- Weekly 30m sync (Mon 09:30) + triage (Fri 16:00)
- Oncall coordination: SREs rotate 2-week shadow with the feature team (explicit handoff doc)

Definitions we use here:
- SLO: availability measured at request-level success (HTTP 2xx + model-safe-response) and latency percentiles per route.
- Error budget: monthly budget derived from SLO; policy defines when rollouts are paused or when capacity increases are triggered.
- Route: a logical API surface (e.g., /v1/generate-chat - gptx-medium-prod)

Pilot route selection criteria (pick 3):
- High request volume (top 30%),
- Externally customer-affecting (non-internal),
- Different failure modes (memory pressure, slow KV, downstream scoring)

Sprint plan (high level)
Week 0 (prep) - discovery and instrument sweep:
- Inventory: owners, deployed variants, existing alerts, dashboards (SREs + platform)
- Quick telemetry gap map: what metrics are missing (trace sampling, per-route latency histograms, kv cache hit rate)
- Deliverable: route inventory sheet + minimal dashboard templates

Week 1-2 - observability and baseline:
- Add per-route tagging to logs (request_id, route, model_version, quantization_profile)
- Deploy synthetic checker (local harness) that hits each route with realistic prompt shapes
- Baseline metrics for 7-day p50/p90/p99, tail latency histograms, and 5xx distribution
- Deliverable: baseline report + proposed SLO targets for each route (example: availability 99.9% monthly, p99 latency 800ms)

Week 3 - error budget automation + rollback policy:
- Implement simple error budget counter (daily rolling window) with alert thresholds: warning at 25% burned, action at 50%, emergency at 80%
- Define automatic rules: pause canary rollouts when burned > 50%; auto-evacuate traffic to fallback when burned > 80%
- Deliverable: error budget alerts in PagerDuty + rollback playbook (doc + checklist)

Week 4 - performance experiments and mitigations:
- Run targeted experiments (one at a time):
  - Enable prefix/KV caching for frequent prompts
  - Adjust batching delta thresholds on serving runtime
  - Try a quantized fallback model for long-tail prompts
- Measure unit-cost delta and latency impact for each change
- Deliverable: experiment log (measurements, configs, links to PRs)

Week 5 - canary + traffic shaping:
- Canary config: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24h at each step and automatic rollback on error budget triggers
- Test outage scenarios: simulate KV outage, node OOM, cold-start storms
- Deliverable: canary runbook + run results

Week 6 - handoff, docs, and playbook publication:
- Finalize step-by-step runbook for each route (how to read SLO dashboards, how to trigger fallback, how to patch runtime configs)
- Publish: Confluence + link from Console guide + add to oncall runbook index
- Deliverable: public playbook, 1 pager for execs summarizing impact and risks removed

Operational primitives we insist on (minimum viable):
- per-route metric tags and tracing
- synthetic checker that mirrors production distribution (not just ping)
- automatable error budget state visible in console + PD alerts
- documented fallback chain (model_variant -> quantized -> cached_response)

Escalation and decision matrix (quick reference):
- Warning (25%): SRE + Feature PM notified, triage in 24h
- Action (50%): Pause rollouts, increase sampling for traces, re-run synthetic test with heavier load
- Emergency (80%): Auto-failover to fallback model & reduce traffic, oncall bridge + customer comms (Customer Success lead notified)

Checklist templates (copy into issues):
- Pre-launch: inventory, baseline metrics, synthetic test green, alerting wired, rollback policy reviewed
- Canary step: monitor p99 and error budget every 6h, snapshot mem/cpu/gpu utilization
- Incident: run brownout script -> escalate -> run fallback -> confirm customer-impact metrics recover

Open questions / trade-offs we must decide quickly:
- SLO cadence: monthly vs 30d rolling. (Recommendation: start with 30d rolling for faster signal.)
- Cost vs latency trade-offs: when to accept higher latency to reduce GPU cost vs maintain p99. (Decision owned by product+finance for each route.)
- Synthetic checker fidelity: how many prompt templates needed to be representative? (Start light: 8 templates, iterate.)

Quick wins (first 2 sprints):
- Add per-route tags to logging and dashboards (low lift, high signal)
- Synthetic checker + baseline report for three routes
- One immediate KV cache tweak that improves p99 for a pilot route

Notes to self / working reminders:
- Keep docs pragmatic, avoid SLO theology in early stage; teams need frictionless adoption.
- Link all experiments to GH PRs and Linear issues (make it easy to revert).
- Capture customer-impact examples for each route (helps PMs prioritize).

Appendix: useful links and templates
- Dashboard template: confluence:dash-templates/sre-slo
- Synthetic checker repo: github.com/redwood-inference/synthetic-checker (WIP branch: field-guide)
- Linear templates: SRV-onboard-slo, SRV-canary-checklist

Action items (first 7 days):
- Ethan: create route inventory, assign owners (due day 2)
- Aisha: prototype per-route log tagging PR (due day 5)
- Daniel: compile product impact list for selected routes (due day 3)
- Maria: spin up synthetic checker dev environment and run baseline scripts (due day 7)

Unresolved: decide whether to include cost burn into error budget calculus (finance input required).

End of field guide (working copy). Expect iterative updates as pilots run. If this doc is useful, convert into a canonical "SLO onramp" doc after 2 pilots succeed.
